title: THE DRUM
sub: This star is from a bronze drum made over two thousand years ago. It is also the logo of this channel. Here is what we know about it.
say: This star is from a bronze drum made over two thousand years ago. It is also the logo of this channel. Here is what we know about it.

title: ĐÔNG SƠN
sub: The drums are named after Đông Sơn, a site in Thanh Hóa province, northern Vietnam, where drums were first excavated in 1924.
say: The drums are named after Dong Sun, a site in Tahn Hwah province, northern Vietnam, where drums were first excavated in nineteen twenty-four.

title: LOST WAX
sub: They were cast in bronze, with techniques that included lost-wax and piece-mold casting. Some stand around a meter tall.
say: They were cast in bronze, with techniques that included lost-wax and piece-mold casting. Some stand around a meter tall.

title: A WIDE WORLD
sub: Bronze drums have been found from southern China across mainland and island Southeast Asia. Their spread suggests contact and exchange.
say: Bronze drums have been found from southern China across mainland and island Southeast Asia. Their spread suggests contact and exchange.

title: WHAT'S ON IT
sub: On some drums, the decorations show birds, boats, stilt houses, and figures wearing feathered headdresses.
say: On some drums, the decorations show birds, boats, stilt houses, and figures wearing feathered headdresses.

title: WHAT FOR?
sub: Their exact role is still uncertain. Some were found in burials, and scholars suggest ceremonial or status-related uses.
say: Their exact role is still uncertain. Some were found in burials, and scholars suggest ceremonial or status-related uses.

title: WHO MADE THEM?
sub: Their origins are debated. Archaeologist Ambra Calò identifies northern Vietnam as a production center. Other scholarship points to Yunnan, where the Dian culture also made bronze drums.
say: Their origins are debated. Archaeologist Ahm-brah Kah-loh identifies northern Vietnam as a production center. Other scholarship points to Yoon-nahn, where the Dee-en culture also made bronze drums.

title: BEYOND BORDERS
sub: Historian Han Xiaorong argues that nationalism and international politics shaped this debate. The drums themselves date from long before modern borders.
